title: Legora partners with Boom Juridisch
summary: Octus credit intelligence is becoming available inside Legora. Benchmark deal terms, speed up restructuring diligence, and support mandate pitches, all cited to the source.
body_markdown:
Dutch legal teams no longer have to choose between trusted content and AI-native research.


Legora today announced a strategic partnership with Boom Juridisch, one of the Netherlands' leading legal publishers and part of Koninklijke Boom uitgevers, a publishing house with a history dating back to 1841. Through this partnership, legal teams with a Boom Juridisch license can run legal research in Legora using Boom Juridisch's authoritative legal content, including handbooks, legal commentary, academic journals, case annotations and scholarly publications.


One of the most frequently expressed needs among legal professionals is the ability to work with trusted, licensed legal content directly within their preferred AI platform. The partnership between Legora and Boom Juridisch responds to this demand, enabling licensed users to bring curated Dutch legal publications into their AI-powered workflows.


Legora's agent combines Dutch primary legal sources, including case law from courts at all levels, legislation, official publications and regulatory materials, with Boom Juridisch's trusted legal scholarship and expert interpretation. This helps legal professionals bridge the gap between finding legal information and understanding and applying it. Every citation links directly to its underlying source.


Boom Juridisch's publishing portfolio covers more than 20 areas of Dutch law, with particular strengths in employment, healthcare, environmental, criminal, corporate, personal injury law and civil procedure. Its publications include the renowned *Advocatenblad* and more than 50 academic and professional legal journals.


The partnership marks another important step in Legora's strategy, announced in September. Legora is rewiring legal research through comprehensive legal data and AI-native navigation built on a full ontology of law that maps relationships across sources, so the Legora agent can see the full picture of current law and navigate it with unprecedented accuracy. By integrating Boom Juridisch’s extensive collection of expert legal publications, Legora further strengthens the depth and quality of the legal content available through its platform.


"Legal teams shouldn't have to choose between the content they trust and the AI platform they want to work in. We are committed to providing the law and the leading commentary on it, in one answer inside Legora. Dutch legal professionals have worked with Boom’s publications for decades. Now Boom’s trusted legal publications are accessible inside the same Legora agent that can access our proprietary ontology to navigate the full body of Dutch case law and legislation,” says Melanie Brown, Senior Director, Legal Data at Legora.


“Legal research is an important part of legal professionals’ day-to-day work. Bringing high-quality academic publications and the latest curated legal updates and analysis into the legal workflow strengthens that research and unlocks the full potential of Boom’s legal portfolio. Legora has proven itself to be an innovative European AI legal workflow provider that supports our vision. We believe that combining quality content with intelligent AI creates the best legal research experience,” says Gerdi Smit, Director Boom Juridisch.


Available for teams with a Boom license, switched on by your Legora team.


**About Boom Juridisch**
Boom Juridisch is a professional and educational legal publisher based in Amsterdam and is part of Koninklijke Boom uitgevers, established in 1841. Boom Juridisch has an extensive portfolio of academic and practice-oriented legal publications, including case law updates in all major fields. It is trusted by nearly all large law firms, as well as a large proportion of smaller and boutique firms.


**About Legora**
Legora is the agentic operating system for legal work, supporting lawyers in research, review, and drafting across complex matters. It is used by more than 150,000 legal professionals at more than 2,500 leading law firms and in-house legal teams across over 80 markets.
